name: Robyn Hitchcock
description: '''Robyn Rowan Hitchcock''' (born 3 March 1953) is an English singer-songwriter and musician. Known for his rich, surrealistic lyrical style and influenced by the [[psychedelic rock]] era, he led [[The Soft Boys]] in the late 1970s before initiating a prolific solo career. He recorded, initially with backing by The Egyptians, for two major American labels ([[A&M Records]] and [[Warner Bros.]]) over the course of the 1980s and 1990s and achieved [[Campus radio|college radio]] success in America. The subject of [[Jonathan Demme]]'s live performance film ''[[Storefront Hitchcock (film)|Storefront Hitchcock]]'' (1998), Hitchcock has been acknowledged a significant influence on [[alternative rock]] and [[Folk music|folk]] performers including [[R.E.M.]] He continues to tour and record prolifically with collaborators including his wife [[Emma Swift]] and retains a dedicated cult following.
